raw_response:
I will still do it the way I know is steady, not too fancy. I have farmed in Quzhou for many years, so I start from what worked last year and only adjust a little. Wheat and maize are my main food and cash from the field, so I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. I have well water, so I am not as scared of dry spells as rain-fed land, but fertilizer still costs real money, so I will not throw it blindly. For wheat, I will put enough base fertilizer so the seedlings stand strong before winter, then I will topdress nitrogen when it turns green in spring. Around here, if wheat fertilizer is too light, the heads stay short and yield falls fast, so I would rather spend a bit more there. For maize, I will use hybrid seed like most people do now, because the stand is better and the ears are more even. I will feed maize a little heavier on nitrogen than wheat, because if maize goes hungry in July and August, it shows immediately. For cotton, I will not plant too much, because it needs more watching and more sprays, and now some family members work outside so labor is tighter than before. I will keep cotton on the lighter area, use better seed, give it potash too, and watch insects closely. I do what I have seen nearby fields do when they get a decent harvest, and I keep my spending balanced so fertilizer does not eat up all the money for pesticide, irrigation, and machine work.
